prompt: In one short sentence: why do sailboats tack against the wind?

delta: Sailboats can't sail straight into the wind, so they zigzag: the sails generate lift when the wind hits them at an angle, and that lift can be turned into forward motion only while the boat is moving off the wind, so a boat tacks back and forth to make progress toward a point upwind.
